notes: ENA project PRJEB36683 contains 1820 Klebsiella samples (including 1554 labelled 'Klebsiella pneumoniae 11227-1'), but the provided paper describes only 328 K. pneumoniae isolates (~18% coverage), limiting most study-level attributes to 'partial'. AMR study type is 'amr' (MDR K. pneumoniae was the explicit entry criterion) but only 'partial' because paper coverage is insufficient (~18%) and the EBI title uses the phrase 'surveillance study', leaving ambiguity about whether all 1820 deposited samples were MDR-selected. AMR target is 'other' because the criterion is MDR (resistance to ≥3 antimicrobial classes), not specifically third-generation cephalosporins or carbapenems. AMR method is primarily 'ast_result' since MDR classification relied on AST; PCR was used supplementarily for species and beta-lactamase gene identification. Cohort age is 'mixed' based on the documented age range of 11–75 years for ST2096 patients (11 falls below the <12 child cutoff). Collection date spans >2 years in the paper (2014–2022), precluding a single backfill date. Country (Saudi Arabia) and host (Homo sapiens) apply whole-project based on EBI metadata and paper context.

In total, we collected 347 new isolates (147 resistant and 200 susceptible isolates; one isolate per patient).

We thus included samples categorized as both intermediate (2 μg/mL) and resistant (≥ 4 μg/mL) by the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute interpretative criteria.

coverage_basis: The paper describes 608 total isolates all deposited under PRJNA271899, corresponding to 1219 ENA samples because each isolate generated both a paired-end and a mate-pair Illumina library (each submitted as a separate biosample entry, consistent with 2800 runs / 1219 samples ≈ 2.3 runs/sample). notes: All 150 ENA samples belong to the genus Klebsiella (taxon of interest). notes: PRJDB17849 is one of four DDBJ BioProjects covering a total of 168 K. pneumoniae clinical strains from Japan (2015–2018); ENA mirrors 0 samples, so project-level sample counts cannot be confirmed from ENA. Isolation was non-AMR-selected (all clinical K. pneumoniae), making this a surveillance study. No age data are available (samples irreversibly de-identified). Collection spans ~3.3 years so a single midpoint collection_date cannot be applied. Multiple specimen types preclude a single isolation_source. Study setting is hospital based on collection at Hiroshima University, Nagoya University Hospital, and MIROKU Medical Laboratory with predominantly blood, respiratory, and urine specimens.
